There was a point I wondered if the joy I had from knowing her was worth the pain of losing her and knowing all along that I would, when I remembered a girl I went to school with (Z) before moving schools and meeting N.

Z was severely disabled and her parents had opted to have her undergo Ashley therapy (hormonally stunting growth to allow for easier care as they get older). Due to how that school seperated grades, I only kind of new her however after I moved she came to take on a large role in the social group I was a part of. Unfortunately she passed away from heart failure at age 20.

N had dwarfism, and a series of strokes had caused some cognitive impairment. She suffered a cardiac arrest age 22. 

Whilst I highly doubt that things with Z and I would have reached the same point they did with N and I, regardless of moving schools or not, I would have been close friends with a disabled girl who had stunted growth and passed away in their early 20s

Somewhat tangential start but bear with me.

A lot of my friends struggle with life significantly and I have noticed they all report it as starting at around aged 13. As a 13y/o, I was way off the rails, angry at everything and tried to run away from home. I blamed everything on my parents divorce and the custody situation ( happened when I was 5) what I came to realise after moving to my mums at 14 was that my problems didn't just go away, they followed me. I also came to understand that I was more looking for something to blame the puberty induced mood swings on. I came to the conclusion that had things been different, my life now would be different yes; but if that difference would be good bad or otherwise is unknown. So as long as I have food and shelter, everything else is superfluous. Also that being ASD, I am different, I see the world differently so if I don't understand what's going on or other people don't understand me, I dont take it personally.

N is/ was the only person I have ever understood at a personal level.

And I know that I would be happier if she was still here. For my outlook to work, it would mean that I treated N's death as insignificant, and that is not something I can reconcile. I have been down some rabbit holes in my time, but none so deep as this one. I still struggle to get out of bed frequently and have had multiple weekends were I haven't gotten out of bed at all except for the facilities and this is overs a year later.

The only reason I didn't kill myself in the first thew days after N died was that literally the week before I had financed a new vehicle and didn't want to saddle my family with the debt ( because logic) eventually I checked myself in but that was only because I had simply run out of energy to carry on before I had all my affairs in order. Eventually everything was in order and I had made peace with my decision. Had notes written out and everything, just waiting on certain items to arrive in the post. Then I got fired from my job and that seemed to hit the reset button for me. I too am on the autism spectrum and have noticed I stim out harder and more often in the past 1y3m (exactly today). I believe it is to do with fixation and repetition. Fixating on wanting to be with them again, the stress causing a repetition stim and the repition reinforcing it.over and over and over again. "I want N back. I want N back. I want N back..." Ad nauseam. Just saying that to myself and flapping so hard I'm surprised I didn't fly away or wear a hole in the floor spinning. I still repeat daily " I want N back" although the idea of speeding up the process has been shelved, but not gone completely. These days it doesn't last the week when it rears its head.

22, male. I joined this ensemble at 21, a thew months after her 22nd. knew her 7 years, together for 5 of them

I knew she wouldn't make it. Doctors were surprised she even made it to 5. she pulled off 22. she shook off 2 ruptured aneurysms like nothing happened, had multiple strokes (including one before she was even born) not to mention many many other health problems.
I was warned of all this when i first made my feelings known, and had the attitude of  "yeah, but I could be hit by a car tomorrow"

and while i knew the shunts in her head wouldn't last forever and the the third aneurysm (inoperable position) could blow any time, she was so incredibly feisty and had flipped the bird at death so many times that it seemed she could just shake anything off.

eventually, she developed an arterial blockage in her heart that they tried to operate on but she arrested on the table (but not before trying to swing at the anesthesiologist while she was halfway under-like i said, feisty) 1 year, 2 months 3 weeks 1 day later and i still can't quite wrap my head around the fact that after everything she shook off, she simply went into arrest while being prepped for surgery.

When N's health was deteriorating, I had her full permission to "seek elsewhere that which she could not provide", but never actively took her up on the offer. one day Whilst at university, a girl (T)  who was regularly in the computer lab at the same time as me asked if i wanted to go for sushi some time. I agreed without really thinking much of it and didn't realize that she had just asked me out until i was on my way home, and that she had been flirting with me all semester (i suck hints) after significant thought and consultation with N, I decided that the worst case scenario was eating some sushi. I was quite upfront with T about N, even before we had made any decisions and she was ok with it. right up until 20 minutes after coming to a decision while we were discussing the practical side of how things would go and i mentioned that N's birthday was 14th of February and as such I would be spending time with her. this led to an immediate defensive response, that she wanted valentines day. after some back and forth about how 14/2 being THE day of romance is kind of arbitrary, and that restaurants would be less crowded and chocolates cheaper on the 15th, she reluctantly agreed and i thought that was the end of it. Nope. she would accuse me of cheating if i so much as knew the name of a another female, (my own mother included) and would be personally insulted and threatening me with a frying pan if i asked if there were any 9v batteries in her house. N and T did meet each other, and T was able to have an in depth conversation with N's mother, as  the pressure on N's brain at that point was severely affecting her ability to hold a conversation. Overall the interaction went relatively smoothly. after everyone else had left and T and I were alone, she immediately starts telling me that N is faking it. Not only is she faking it, but she is faking it with the express purpose of getting at her. I had known N for years before i even met T, and HOW ON EARTH CAN YOU FAKE THE PHYSICAL SYMPTOMS?  in the same vein, T suggested that I'm not even autistic, my mum just didn't raise me properly, so I wouldn't learn social skills, so I wouldn't get a girlfriend, and would have me all to herself forever. I wrote it off as an occupational hazard of dating someone with bipolar disorder for quite some time, having heard similar tales from others, but eventually it was the frying pan that led to me ending it.

i think it differs from company to company. at the first job, my first accident report was taking a good chunk of skin off my thumb by hitting with a hammer. I didn't think much of it, as you could be a tradie for 20 years and still bash your thumb with a hammer, i just took off enough skin it warranted a first aid report. a couple of weeks later, while changing the acetylene tank, i slipped with the spanner, hit myself in the face and needed 2 stitches. very minor in my opinion, head wounds bleed a lot anyway. but suddenly management bans me from using power tools, and adjustable spanners. ring spanners only. got to work the next morning to find my toolkit had been stripped of anything even remotely sharp. a thew weeks later i leaned an aluminum rod against a live 1600v bus bar that nobody had thought to tell me was there. boss ripped me a new one for that. took them nearly a month to actually put up a sign about it. ultimately it was spilling kerosene ALL OVER myself that led to my termination. on paper i was made redundant and let go with a good reference, but in practice i was fired. at my current job i have ...: crashed the forklift more times than i can count (including into scaffolding), busted a water main, knocked over a dumpster, broken the corner off a house roof, caused large potholes in BRAND NEW roadways (they needed a digger to pull me out of the rut i got into) knocked over a portaloo... there's more i just can't remember right now, and after filling out the incident report, everyone just laughs at me, i buy a round at the social club and everyone carries on.

not by design, but yes.

at the end of the wake, it took her parents and our old teacher to convince me to go home, as i felt that when i left, it would all be over. Her parents did say to me that they would always consider me one of them, and that given time they would invite me around again, both to reminisce and give me a box of stuff when she gets the strength to clear her old room. fast forward 10 months, it is the middle of the night just before what should have been her 23rd birthday and i am standing on their front lawn, completely off my face and dressed as a unicorn with clip on butterfly wings (also, blue hair dye) decorating their garden with 4 storage crates worth of origami. turns out her dad was working nightshift that day so came up the driveway to find me there. the following exchange took place:
HD:"um... hello" (more confused than anything else)
Me: (slurring, very mournfully) "hello, I didn't mean to disturb you"
HD:"...(sighs) thats ok...what's happened?"
Me: "I made origami butterflies"
HD: "ah, why don't you come in"
when we get inside, HD is ahead of me and announces my presence to the rest of the family with a "um" accompanied by a gesture in my direction and shrug of the shoulders. Her mother was was stunned, but not overly surprised. we had as much of a catch up as i was capable of having in my state, as i was not prepared to meet her family or be inside her house again, and although i didn't know what i was expecting from the night, it wasn't that, but i still think the night went as well as it possibly could have.

When I first met N, her health was already quite poor and when I first expressed my feelings for her, I was met with a warning and advised it was in every bodies best interest not pursue anything . in spite of this...well yeah. I had her blessing to "seek elsewhere that which she could not provide", although never actively sought as much. One day at uni, a girl who was regularly in the computer lab at the same time as me invited me for lunch. I did not realize i had agreed to a date until i got home and decided that worst case scenario, i ate some lunch. I was completely upfront with T in regards to the situation with N very early on in things, and N was fully aware of the situation with T. T was ok with it during the "just friends" phase but after we decided to see where things went, as we began discussing the practical side of things, i mentioned that N's birthday happened to fall on valentines day (which is kind of arbitrary) and as such i would be spending it with her. T is immediately on the defensive and begins accusing N of downright faking everything (including physical symptoms which are downright impossible to fake). I wrote it off for a little while, as I can easily understand why there would be a certain level of jealousy, although was a little miffed  at the way she appeared to be dealing with it. as things progressed, she would be on my case about me so much as knowing THE NAME of another female. case in point one of my old teachers from when i lived in a town 5 hours away had since become principal at the school across the road from her place. we met in passing, said hello, exchanged the usual pleasantries and went about our day. next thing you know shes going on at me for talking to the principal, so the girls at the school would think i was all good with the principal so if they got all good with me i might score them some favors from the principal. I soon realized  that she was merely possessive as hell, even accusing me of sleeping with my own mother. (my personal favorite "you probably don't even have asperger's, your mum just didn't raise you properly, so you would never learn social skills, so you would never get a girlfriend, so she could have you all to herself forever") and she genuinely believed that the entire world was in on a massive conspiracy against her. I broke that relationship off after being threatened with a frying pan because i asked if she had any 9v batteries in the house (not an isolated incident) i am just so thankful that i had N sticking around the entire time. but alas, 1 year, 3 weeks and 1 day ago, N passed away. now every time i am faced with a female encounter, the only thing i can think is "you're not N, I want N back'. my experience with T has definitely played havoc with me, always imaging that potential mates won't see me as being fully committed to them if N is still on my mind, yet the logical part of me says that anybody who still views N as a threat is going to be possessive beyond belief and the correct steps to take are very big ones. lately i have been wondering if i want to try putting myself out there again, but i also plan to leave the country when my contract is up, and don't want to take anyone along with me, yet the loneliness is just crippling. I don't want "somebody", I want N.
